settings._action_note: Playbook actions are defined ONLY in the operator profile overlay (STEEL_INTEL_PROFILE_JSON / config/profile.json). This public file must never contain an `action` key: an action names the company's licences and is private by construction. See src/playbook.py.
settings._push_budget_note: LINE bills (requests x recipients), NOT message objects: one request carries up to 5 text objects of ~4,900 chars for the price of one. Arithmetic: line_monthly_quota/line_recipients = 300/2 = 150 requests per month; summary_reserve_per_day (3 digests) x 31 days = 93 reserved, leaving ~57 requests/month for realtime alerts (~2/day = alert_push_budget_per_day). A whole cycle of alerts is packed into ONE request, so this budget is per CYCLE, not per news item. When the daily budget is spent, only alert_override_levels items may still fire, at most alert_override_max_per_day extra requests; everything else waits for the next cycle or the daily digest (nothing is dropped). quota_warn_ratio: append a quota warning to the digest once the month passes this fraction of the plan.
settings._lookback_note: Freshness window: an article whose actual publication time is older than this many hours is ignored (never stored/alerted), regardless of dedup state. Comparison is timezone-aware in Asia/Bangkok.
settings._drop_if_no_date_note: When an item has NO parseable published date (e.g. gov listing links): false = keep it (conservative, preserves gov signal), true = drop it (strict).
settings._cluster_note: Same-story collapse at DISPLAY time only (src/cluster.py): rows are never merged or deleted in the database, they are only grouped when a card or a digest is built, and every outlet in a group is still named on the card. cluster_jaccard_min is the character-3-gram overlap two headlines need to count as one story. 0.62 was chosen from real headlines in this DB: one story re-worded by another desk measures 0.62-1.00, while the dangerous near-miss pair (different events, same actors, same vocabulary) 'ผู้ผลิตเตา IF ค้านแนวคิด กมอ.' vs 'สมาคมเหล็ก IF โวย มติ กมอ.' measures 0.15 - so 0.62 sits in the middle of the empty band, not on the edge of either group. Lower it to 0.55 to merge more aggressively, but ALWAYS run `python main.py --cluster-report` first and read every group it prints: a wrong merge hides real news. cluster_ratio_min is difflib's order-aware second opinion, cluster_len_ratio_min stops a short headline being swallowed by a long one, cluster_window_hours refuses to merge the same headline published days apart (that is a re-run, i.e. new news), cluster_max_rows disables collapsing on an unexpectedly huge batch (grouping is O(rows x groups)), and cluster_enabled=false restores the previous behaviour exactly.

settings._priority_alert_note: Critical keywords so central to this company's survival (TIS standards on rebar / IF furnaces, and anti-dumping measures) that a YELLOW item mentioning one still fires an instant alert instead of waiting for the daily digest. Everything else still needs RED/ORANGE. Rationale: the 2026-08-26 headline 'ขยับ 4 มอก. เป็นสินค้าควบคุม' scored exactly 4 (YELLOW) and would have been silently digested.
settings._archive_note: The public back-catalogue site (src/archive.py, built by `python main.py --build-archive`). It is meant to sit on GitHub Pages in a PUBLIC repository, so every page is built from audience.public_rows() ONLY - the headline, source, time, link, level and topics - and never from impact notes, score, matched keywords or the watchlist. Each page is rendered in memory and audited (profile sentences + forbidden field names) BEFORE anything is written; one hit aborts the whole build and no file is written at all. archive_index_max_kb caps the payload embedded in the FRONT PAGE only: older news is not dropped, it stays on its quarter page, which always holds every row (the index is a shortcut, never the only copy). archive_include_level=false publishes the news without the RED/ORANGE/YELLOW reading of it. archive_url is the public address of the built site: while it is EMPTY the digest does not change by a single byte - nothing links to the archive until this is filled in deliberately.
settings._watchlist_alert_note: Proactive watchlist deadline reminders (src/reminder.py). The digest has always carried a passive countdown, and that stopped working: the AD wire-rod entry has printed the same overdue line on every digest since June, three rounds a day, and nobody acted on it. watchlist_warn_days lists the days-BEFORE-deadline on which an entry speaks up; once the deadline has passed it repeats every watchlist_overdue_repeat_days instead of every round. Deliberately sparse - a reminder on every digest is the very problem this setting fixes. The block is FULL-AUDIENCE ONLY (it names watchlist titles, which are private for the same reason the countdown is) and it rides inside a digest that is already being sent, so it costs ZERO extra LINE requests. Repeats within one day are blocked by a meta key (wl_nudge_<id>_<date>) because digests run 3x/day. Set watchlist_warn_days to [] to turn the pre-deadline half off; nothing shows at all when no entry is due, and the digest is then byte-for-byte what it was before this feature existed.
settings._audience_note: Who gets what (src/audience.py). The private channel (LINE_USER_ID push) receives the FULL version: impact notes, score, matched keywords and the watchlist. The OA broadcast receives the PUBLIC version: the same headlines, sources, times, links and 'also reported by' blocks, without this operator's reading of them. team_digest_rounds lists the hours whose daily digest is also broadcast to the team; a round later than the last hour in this list still sends if the team has not been served today (catch-up, because loop.yml hands over roughly every 5 hours and the 18:00 round can fall inside a handover). team_realtime_alerts=true additionally broadcasts instant alerts, which is off by default: realtime fires far more often and would eat the quota. Push arithmetic: LINE bills (requests x recipients) per destination, so a day with a private channel and one team round costs 3 private digests + 1 broadcast. line_team_recipients is how many people have added the OA - it is REPORTING ONLY (shown by `python main.py --audience`); the budget maths in src/quota.py stays on line_recipients.
